answer: Each PoA identity must complete a challenge-bound kernel of sequential modular squarings before it can produce a Wesolowski proof. Because every step depends on the previous one, GPUs cannot divide one chain into parallel work or remove its elapsed-time bottleneck; they can run separate clone chains, but each consumes resources and time. The spiral of cloned identities therefore raises cost, while the proof lets peers verify completion without repeating the work—a pearl of compact evidence.
